description: Original synthetic development corpus. Not held-out real-world evidence. Splits frozen by concept/source group.

documents.text: A recursive function calls itself. A base case ends the recursion before another recursive call. Without a reachable base case, calls can exhaust the stack.
A hash table maps keys to buckets using a hash function. Collisions occur when different keys map to the same bucket. Chaining stores multiple entries in that bucket.
An inner SQL join returns rows with matching keys in both tables. A left join also retains unmatched rows from the left table and fills missing right-side values with nulls.
A database transaction groups changes into one logical unit. Atomicity means all changes commit together or none do. Isolation controls interference between concurrent transactions.
Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search interval. Its worst-case comparison count grows logarithmically with the number of elements. The input must be sorted.
A regression test checks that a previously working behavior has not broken. A unit test isolates a small component, while an integration test exercises collaborating components.
The derivative of a function describes its instantaneous rate of change. Geometrically it is the slope of the tangent line at a point where the derivative exists.
A definite integral accumulates signed contributions over an interval. Regions below the horizontal axis contribute negative signed area. Absolute geometric area requires accounting for sign changes.
An eigenvector of a square matrix keeps its direction under the matrix transformation, apart from possible reversal. The associated eigenvalue is its scale factor.
Bayes theorem updates a prior probability using observed evidence and a likelihood. The posterior probability depends on both the prior and how probable the evidence is under the hypothesis.
Variance measures the average squared deviation from the mean. Squaring prevents positive and negative deviations from cancelling. Standard deviation is the square root of variance.
The gradient of a differentiable scalar function points toward its steepest local increase under the Euclidean norm. Gradient descent steps in the opposite direction to reduce the objective locally.

Fine-tuning starts from pretrained model weights and continues training on task-specific examples. It can require less task data than training from scratch because useful representations were learned earlier.
Overfitting occurs when a model captures peculiarities of training data that do not generalize. A widening gap between training and validation performance can indicate overfitting.

Self-attention computes context-dependent representations by weighting other tokens in a sequence. Attention weights depend on query and key comparisons, and the resulting weighted sum uses value vectors.
A text embedding represents text as a vector. Semantic retrieval compares query and passage vectors, often with cosine similarity. Similar vectors can retrieve differently worded descriptions.

A calibrated probabilistic classifier has predictions that agree with observed frequencies. Among many cases assigned probability 0.7, approximately 70 percent should be positive if the model is calibrated.
Data leakage happens when training uses information unavailable at prediction time. Splitting related chunks from one document across train and test can give overly optimistic evaluation results.
Inflation is a sustained increase in a general price index. It differs from a rise in the price of one isolated item. This note states a definition, not a current inflation rate.
Opportunity cost is the value of the best forgone alternative. Choosing to study for one hour can sacrifice an hour available for another valued activity.
Price elasticity of demand compares the percentage change in quantity demanded to the percentage change in price. Elastic demand has a larger quantity response in percentage terms.
Gross domestic product measures the value of final goods and services produced within an economy during a period. Intermediate inputs are excluded to avoid double counting.
An externality is a cost or benefit affecting a third party outside a transaction. Pollution can impose costs on nearby residents who are not parties to the production contract.
Comparative advantage means producing a good at a lower opportunity cost than another producer. Absolute advantage concerns productivity rather than opportunity cost.
Retrieval practice asks learners to recall information rather than only reread it. A closed-book attempt reveals gaps that may be hidden by familiarity with the page.
Spaced practice distributes review over time instead of concentrating every repetition in one session. A scheduler can shorten the next interval after unsuccessful recall.
Interleaved practice mixes related problem types. Choosing which method applies is part of the exercise, whereas blocked practice repeats one problem type at a time.
Useful learning feedback identifies an error and suggests a next action. A correctness score alone does not necessarily explain the reason for the mistake.
A correct answer produced after a hint is evidence of assisted performance. It should be distinguished from independent recall when deciding what to review.
Metacognition includes monitoring what one knows and choosing learning strategies. Comparing predicted quiz performance with actual results can reveal inaccurate self-assessment.
A news story has a publication date and may describe an earlier event date. A recently retrieved page can still contain old information. Retrieval time alone does not establish currency.
A correction changes a previously published account. A memory system should retain provenance and show which version supports an answer instead of silently mixing old and corrected claims.
Attribution identifies who made a claim and where it was reported. A quotation demonstrates what a source said but does not independently prove that the statement is true.
Correlation describes association between variables. Establishing a causal effect requires additional assumptions or evidence beyond observing that two trends move together.
A survey result depends on its sampling method and who responded. A large convenience sample can still be biased if some parts of the population are systematically missing.
A responsible report distinguishes confirmed observations from estimates and speculation. Numerical estimates should retain their uncertainty and the date or conditions to which they apply.
